name: Mattaniah
overview: Mattaniah was a male descendant of Elam noted in the book of Ezra for having married a foreign wife. The tribe and additional personal details about Mattaniah are not recorded in Scripture. His mention highlights the challenges faced by the post-exilic community in maintaining covenantal purity.
namesAndTitles: The name Mattaniah means "gift of YHWH," reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges God's gracious provision. This proper name is recorded in Ezra 10:26 without indication that it was given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Mattaniah as a descendant of Elam. Beyond this lineage, no other family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Mattaniah's significance lies in his representation of the issue of intermarriage with foreign wives among the returned exiles. His inclusion in Ezra 10:26 underscores the community's effort to restore faithfulness to God's covenant by addressing such marriages. This episode serves as a reminder of the importance of holiness and obedience in God's redemptive plan.
